```{r, include = FALSE}
has_asreml <- requireNamespace("asreml", quietly = TRUE)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 5)
```

This workflow fits a genomic factor analytic (FA) model to a simulated
multi-environment trial (MET) and uses the FAST selection tools of Smith &
Cullis (2018). ASReml-R is licensed software; chunks that need it are only run
when it is installed`r if (!has_asreml) " (it was not available when this vignette was built, so no model output is shown)"`.

```{r setup}
library(UtilityFunctions)
```

## 1. Simulate and check the data

`generate_genomic_met()` draws two latent factors from a genomic relationship
matrix and lays each site out as a randomised complete block design.

```{r data}
G <- generate_grm(n_gen = 80, n_markers = 500, seed = 1)$grm
met <- generate_genomic_met(n_sites = 6, grm = G, n_reps = 2, h2 = 0.6, seed = 1)
met$Genotype <- factor(as.character(met$Genotype), levels = rownames(G))

validate_met_data(met, trait = "Yield", genotype = "Genotype", env = "Site")
conn <- check_met_connectivity(met, trial_col = "Site", gen_col = "Genotype")
```

## 2. Fit the FA model

```{r fit, eval = has_asreml}
model <- asreml::asreml(
  Yield ~ Site,
  random = ~ fa(Site, 2):vm(Genotype, G),
  residual = ~ dsum(~ units | Site),
  data = met, trace = FALSE, maxit = 40
)
model <- mkConv(model)
```

## 3. Extract, rotate and rank

`fa.asreml()` reads the loadings, specific variances and scores of the FA term,
applies the SVD rotation and computes overall performance (OP) and stability
(RMSD). Supplying the relationship matrix `G` gives reliabilities on the
correct scale, \(r^2_g = 1 - \mathrm{PEV}/g_{ii}\).

```{r extract, eval = has_asreml}
fa <- fa.asreml(model, grm = G)
summary(fa)
head(rank_genotypes(fa, weight_stability = 1))
```

## 4. Visualise

```{r plots, eval = has_asreml}
plot(fa, type = "fast")
plot(fa, type = "vaf")
plot(fa, type = "biplot")
plot(fa, type = "latent_reg", factor = 2)
```

## 5. Interaction classes

Environments are grouped by the sign of their factor-2 loadings, and each
genotype gets a predicted performance within each class.

```{r iclass, eval = has_asreml}
ic <- calculate_i_classes(fa, factors = 2)
ic$environments
head(ic$genotypes[order(-ic$genotypes$iClassOP), ])
```
